# Schedule Baseline and Variance

A **baseline** is a frozen copy of the plan, taken before tracking starts, that later reality is
measured against. Without it a schedule has no memory: the current plan always looks correct,
because it has silently absorbed every change. Variance is the difference between the frozen copy
and the live one, and it only exists because the copy was kept.

This is the same discipline as [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]], applied to a schedule
rather than to source files — the superseded version is what makes the delta legible.

## The frozen copy and the delta

[[computer-project-management]] captures the baseline at lab 5–6 and then reports against it:

| | Baseline | Current | Variance |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Duration | 123 d | 134 d | **+11 d** |
| Work | 2 640 h | 2 888 h | +248 h |
| Cost | 176 080 zł | 190 960 zł | **+14 880 zł** |

Finish moves 24 Aug → 8 Sep 2026. The cost variance is not an overspend decision — it is +248 hours
at the same hourly rates, because the budget in this plan is 100 % labour. Duration, work and cost
are one number expressed three ways.

## Progress reported three ways, deliberately

At the June reporting date: **37 %** complete by duration, **31 %** by work (908 of 2 888 h),
**30.7 %** of cost incurred. Three different denominators giving three different answers is the
point — duration is ahead of work because the completed phases were the short, thinly-staffed ones.
A single "percent complete" would hide that.

The seven zero-day milestones from the [[work-breakdown-structure]] carry the per-phase status
(*Preparatory* ✓, *Database* ✓, *Platform* late, four pending), so the aggregate percentages are
attributable rather than free-floating.

## What is measured, and what is not

The repo reports **raw deltas only**. There is no earned-value analysis anywhere in the readable
files — no CPI, no SPI, no EAC, no cost or schedule performance index. That is a real limitation
rather than an oversight to fill in: with 30.7 % of cost spent against 37 % of duration elapsed,
CPI/SPI would say something the raw deltas do not, and nothing in the repo says it.

Nor is there a risk register or any probabilistic estimate — see [[critical-path-method]] on the
absence of PERT.

## Attribution of the variance

The +11 days are traced to a named cause rather than left as a number: four tasks extended, most
importantly unit testing at +16 days, plus the resequencing recorded as
[[sequence-integration-after-unit-testing]]. Sixteen days of extension yielding eleven days of slip
is float being consumed — see [[critical-path-method]].
